questions.question: What is design QA and how is it different from regular functional QA testing?
questions.answer_summary: Design QA is described as a cross-verification process done by designers to check that the built product matches the intended design (visual consistency, spacing, interactions), distinct from functional/bug testing.

questions.question: When in a project should design QA start?
questions.answer_summary: As soon as functional prototypes exist — guidance recommends starting review 'the moment you get your hands on functional prototypes' rather than waiting until final pre-launch.

questions.question: Why do small teams often skip or shortchange design QA?
questions.answer_summary: Cited reasons include the misconception that a designer's job ends at handoff, time pressure limiting review iterations, and friction between designers and developers over feedback.

questions.question: What should be on a pre-launch design QA checklist?
questions.answer_summary: Recommended checks include visual consistency (spacing/alignment/styles across pages), responsive behavior across desktop/tablet/mobile, no leftover placeholder content, working forms/links, mobile tap-target sizing, and correct staging/domain/SSL setup.

questions.question: Is it worth spending extra designer time before launch to avoid developer rework after?
questions.answer_summary: Industry framing argues yes: 'a few extra hours of your designers is better than a few extra days of your developers' hunting down inconsistencies post-release.

questions.question: Does design QA need to check accessibility, not just visual polish?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — accessibility compliance is listed as one of the essential design QA checklist components alongside visual consistency and interaction behavior.

questions.question: What non-visual technical items should be checked right before a website launch?
questions.answer_summary: Items include verifying the staging environment, connecting the custom domain, enabling SSL, and configuring analytics/third-party integrations.
